clue.text: Weapons four girls carry

indicators.note: the girls hold the four within them, as if carrying it inside

parts.note: unmarried young women are misses
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four young women are armed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the girls carry weapons; in fact MISSES carries IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically a missive was anything thrown, such as a missile, so missive weapons are projectiles.

clue.text: Bringing luck to a great many at the races?

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many
Ascot is the famous English racecourse and its royal race meeting

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a big crowd at the racecourse brings good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, whose summer meeting is a social event. The definition is loose: a lucky charm is a thing that brings luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept as a charm for good fortune.

clue.text: Giving flyer kiss, in excitement

indicators.note: in excitement the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gives a pilot a kiss in a moment of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitement' shakes up KISS and IN. 'flyer' suggests an aviator but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small finch, a bird and so a flyer.

clue.text: Portuguese decapitated Russian

indicators.note: beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Siberian is a person from Siberia, part of Russia

explanation.surface: A Portuguese person beheaded a Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the S from the front of SIBERIAN. 'Portuguese' is an adjective here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal shares the Iberian peninsula with Spain, so anything Portuguese is Iberian.

clue.text: Strips quietly off, with the swimmers

indicators.note: the soft letter is taken off the word for strips

parts.note: peels means strips, as skin from fruit
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone undresses discreetly to go bathing with others.
explanation.walkthrough: PEELS less P leaves the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are snakelike fish, creatures that swim.

clue.text: Warded off the boy

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy was fended off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the letters of WARDED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is a boy's name.

clue.text: Sprinkles a little water on the sheep folds

parts.note: a dam is the mother of a farm animal such as a sheep
folds are enclosures for sheep, pens

explanation.surface: A farmer splashes water over the sheep pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folds' looks like a verb but is the noun for sheep enclosures.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen is to moisten something slightly.

clue.text: One means of making potpourri of flowers

indicators.note: a potpourri is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests a way to make potpourri from blossoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potpourri' really is made of flowers, but here signals the letters of ONE MEANS are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are spring flowers of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Not so elated? Definitely not!

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are definitely not to be read in their printed order, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: Asked if they are less than cheerful, someone emphatically denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: rearranged SO ELATED gives a word for very far from elated.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means utterly miserable and forlorn, the opposite of being cheerful.

clue.text: Is better half devious about not being wifely?

indicators.note: the devious word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sly means devious, cunning

indicators.note: half of the word better is taken, here its second half

explanation.surface: A wife asks whether her husband is being devious about her lack of wifeliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better half' looks like a spouse but means half of the word 'better'; 'about' signals the wrap, and the definition jokes that a sister is not a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a sibling sister rather than a wife is the joke behind the loose definition.

clue.text: Treaty town but name is garbled

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes a town famous for a treaty has had its name mangled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Treaty of Amiens (1802) briefly made peace between Britain and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a French city that gave its name to the 1802 peace treaty.

clue.text: Frenchman willing to ring the whole world

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a Frenchman
on means willing, as in I'm on for that
to dial is to ring on a telephone

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is ready to telephone everyone on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase for an adjective: mondial means relating to the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: Mondial, from French monde, means worldwide or global.

clue.text: Nothing for equipment in the beginning

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: In the beginning there was nothing in place of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link here, and 'in' supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the starting point or source of something.

clue.text: Student got up to politely acknowledge first prize award, maybe

indicators.note: the rising and the bowing come first, before the student

parts.note: rose means got up
to bow is to acknowledge someone politely
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A student stands to bow at winning top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car. A rose bowl is a decorative bowl often given as a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a silver bowl commonly presented as a trophy at shows.

clue.text: Works hard in the French stock-exchange, mainly

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: the Bourse is the Paris stock exchange

explanation.surface: Someone toils on the floor of the Paris stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of BOURSE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour is to work hard, so labours means toils.

clue.text: Within metal container on the way to earth, it's white-hot

parts.note: in means within
a can is a tin, a metal container
a descent is a coming down towards the ground

explanation.surface: Something in a tin falling to the ground is glowing with heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing from intense heat.

clue.text: Outline for performance — turn in a score

indicators.note: to turn the letters is to rework them into another order

explanation.surface: A performer plans to slip a turn into a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' and 'score' suggest music hall, but 'turn' just rearranges IN A SCORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline plot of a play or film.

clue.text: Less firm footing, I found, wearing an 'unsupportive shoe

indicators.note: the shoe is worn around the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a slipper is a soft shoe giving little support

explanation.surface: Someone finds their soft shoes make them more prone to slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I found' reads as narrative; I is just placed inside SLIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippier means more slippery, giving less secure footing.

clue.text: Neckband restricts moving in a robot, but is supportive

indicators.note: the neckband holds the other letters in, restricting them

parts.note: a collar is a band round the neck

indicators.note: moving letters around rearranges them

explanation.surface: A robot's collar restricts its movement, yet it remains helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges 'a robot' and 'restricts' has the neckband hold those letters. The definition is loose: a collaborator is one who is supportive.
explanation.definitionFit: A collaborator works jointly with and helps another person.

clue.text: Business interests -—- they can be romantic too

explanation.surface: Commercial concerns may turn into love interests.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both public matters of business and private love liaisons.

clue.text: Troops not in mail

parts.note: out means not in
post means mail

explanation.surface: Soldiers are absent when the letters arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an outpost is a detachment of troops stationed at a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small military position, or the soldiers posted there.

clue.text: The French wine having potential

parts.note: la is French for the
tent is a Spanish red wine

explanation.surface: A French wine shows promise.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red Spanish wine, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent exists in hidden form and could yet develop.

clue.text: Newsman tried rampaging about nothing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the zero
rampaging means wild, so the letters run riot

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A journalist ran amok over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampaging' turns TRIED into EDITR, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor runs a newspaper, so is a newsman.

clue.text: Pile I fashion is turnip-shaped

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth
to form is to fashion

explanation.surface: Someone sculpts a heap into the shape of a root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like an anagram signal but is FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Napiform comes from Latin napus, a turnip, plus form: shaped like a turnip root.

clue.text: Bear crossing river to shore

indicators.note: the bear word goes across the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to stand is to bear or tolerate

explanation.surface: A bear wades over a river to reach the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a beach or the land along water's edge.

clue.text: Low joint where a cap is worn

definitions.text: Low joint where a cap is worn

parts.words: Low joint where a cap is worn
parts.note: a leg joint down low that carries a bony cap, not a pub where hats are worn

explanation.surface: A cheap bar where customers keep their hats on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a seedy bar and 'cap' a hat; the cap is the patella.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is a low leg joint covered by the kneecap.

clue.text: Though dried, is in the wet

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rain is the wet weather

explanation.surface: Something stays dry even out in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a dried grape sitting in wet weather; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape.

clue.text: In the strait, it's offensive

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: Something in a narrow channel is objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The SOLENT is the strait separating the Isle of Wight from Hampshire in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and disrespectful, offensive in manner.

clue.text: Hours, writhing in extreme pain, with this attack

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the jumbled letters
writhing means twisting about, so the letters are rearranged
an extreme of a word is an end letter, here the last

explanation.surface: Someone writhes for hours in severe pain from an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' turns HOURS into ORUSH, and 'in' puts the last letter of 'pain', N, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a forward surge, a charge or assault.

clue.text: Getting the leaver to try switching rota

parts.note: to test is to try

indicators.note: switching the letters round puts them in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to rearrange a duty schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaver' is one who leaves an estate in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, leaving property to heirs.
